title: How Are Others Interpreting What You Say and Do
author: Admired Leadership
summary: Starting from the communication-theory idea that people "cannot NOT communicate," this article argues every behavior conveys meaning across three simultaneous dimensions: task, identity, and relationship. It explains that listeners instantly form judgments about what needs to get done, who the communicator is as a person, and where the relationship stands, whether or not the speaker intends to send those signals. The piece critiques leaders who focus solely on the task and later try to repair identity or relationship damage after the fact, arguing that sequencing doesn't work, all three must be addressed within the same message. It closes by urging leaders to drop the illusion that how they're perceived is outside their control, since every interaction is already shaping all three judgments at once.
points: Every behavior communicates on three simultaneous dimensions, task, identity, and relationship, whether or not the speaker intends it.
Leaders who focus exclusively on the task often discover, to their surprise, that colleagues view them negatively on identity or relationship grounds.
Attempting to repair identity or relationship damage after the fact doesn't work as well as integrating all three goals into the original message.
The article urges leaders to abandon the idea that how they're perceived is beyond their control, since perception forms almost instantly in every interaction.
quotes: A popular maxim among communication professionals is that people “cannot NOT communicate.
Of the many possible readings people make of your behavior, three stand out for their importance: task, identity, and relationship.
At the same time, the message or behavior also communicates and reinforces the identity or social image of the communicator.
The best communicators are thoughtful about the three interpretations others make and attempt to be mindful of doing things that convey how they want to be viewed.
Only messages that balance all three components have the potential to create the positive interpretations good people want and desire from others.
